name: SSRF protection
needs: my app fetches a URL the user pastes in
users can set their own webhook URL
import an image from a URL
summary: Guarding any feature where your server fetches a URL that a user supplied. Without it, someone can point your server at internal addresses, like a cloud metadata endpoint or an admin panel on localhost, and read the response through your app.
need_when: Link previews, 'import from URL', user-set webhook URLs, PDF or screenshot rendering of user URLs, or an AI tool that browses.
skip_when: Your server only calls fixed URLs that you wrote in the code.

ways.title: Resolve, check, then connect to that IP
ways.how: Allow only https, resolve the host, reject any private, loopback, link-local or reserved address, then connect to the checked IP so a second DNS answer can't swap it. Don't follow redirects, or check each hop the same way.
ways.tradeoff: Strong. Easy to get subtly wrong, so use a tested helper and test it.

ways.title: An outbound proxy with rules
ways.how: Send user-URL fetches through a proxy like Smokescreen that blocks internal ranges, and give the app no other route out for those calls.
ways.tradeoff: One choke point for every feature. Another service to run.

ways.title: An allowlist of domains
ways.how: Only fetch from a known list, like the image hosts or integrations you support.
ways.tradeoff: Safest. Too narrow for general link previews.

prompt:
Add SSRF protection to every place this app fetches a user-supplied URL ([features]).

Requirements:
- One shared fetch helper. All user-URL fetches go through it.
- Allow only https (http only in local development). Reject URLs with a username or password in them.
- Resolve the hostname with a time limit, and reject if any resolved address is private, loopback, link-local (including 169.254.169.254), multicast or reserved, for both IPv4 and IPv6.
- Connect to the IP you checked, not the hostname again, to block DNS rebinding.
- Don't follow redirects, or re-run every check on each redirect target with a limit of [3].
- Set a total timeout of [10] seconds and a response size cap of [1 MB].
- Never return raw error details or the internal response to the user.

Acceptance checks (run each and show me the result):
1. http://127.0.0.1, http://localhost and http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/ are all rejected.
2. A hostname that resolves to 10.0.0.5 is rejected.
3. A public URL that redirects to an internal address is rejected.
4. IPv6 forms like http://[::1]/ are rejected.
5. A slow server is cut off at the timeout, and a huge response at the size cap.
acceptance_checks: http://127.0.0.1, http://localhost and http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/ are all rejected.
A hostname that resolves to 10.0.0.5 is rejected.
A public URL that redirects to an internal address is rejected.
IPv6 forms like http://[::1]/ are rejected.
A slow server is cut off at the timeout, and a huge response at the size cap.
if_you_skip_it: Attackers read cloud credentials from the metadata service, reach internal admin tools, or scan your private network through your app.
how_derek_runs_it: Custody Journal's outgoing webhooks go through an SSRF guard. It requires https (http only in debug), rejects URLs with embedded credentials, resolves the host with a 5 second limit, and refuses if any resolved address isn't a public one. It then connects to the checked IP, never follows redirects, and caps each call at 10 seconds and a 64 KB response.
